<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Errors

Every error response has the same shape:

```json
{"error": {"code": "REG-1007", "name": "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "message": "claude-opus is not allowed on tier standard"}}
```

The `code` is stable and safe to match on in code; the `message` is for people and may change. The full list is in the error code reference.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Errors

Every error response has the same shape:

```json
{"error": {"code": "REG-1007", "name": "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "message": "claude-opus is not allowed on tier standard"}}
```

The `code` is stable and safe to match on in code; the `message` is for people and may change. The full list is in the error code reference.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

|---|---|

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.

## How do I find out which model my agent is on?

Look it up in the registry: its record has a `model` field. If you're writing code that runs as the agent, ask the registry "who am I?" with the agent's own key and you'll get the same record back.

<source id="D01:6" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Deleting an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Deleting an agent

`DELETE /agents/{agent_id}` removes an agent's record permanently. Prefer setting `status` to `retired`, which keeps the record and its change history. Delete only agents that were created by mistake.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Errors

Every error response has the same shape:

```json
{"error": {"code": "REG-1007", "name": "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "message": "claude-opus is not allowed on tier standard"}}
```

The `code` is stable and safe to match on in code; the `message` is for people and may change. The full list is in the error code reference.
</source>

|---|---|

## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D14:1" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Can my agent use the biggest model?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Can my agent use the biggest model?

Only on the priority tier. Standard-tier agents can use the smaller and mid-sized models. Moving to priority needs a sign-off from whoever holds your team's budget, and after that you can change the model.

## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.

## Prometheus Agent Mode

The Agent mode optimizes Prometheus for the remote write use case. It disables querying, alerting, and local storage and replaces it with a customized TSDB WAL. Everything else stays the same: scraping logic, service discovery, and related configuration. It can be used as a drop-in replacement for Prometheus if you want to just forward your data to a remote Prometheus server or any other Remote-Write-compliant project.

</source>

<source id="D02:3" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Monitoring errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Monitoring errors

These come from the monitoring service, not from the Registry API, but they appear in the same alert channels.

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MON-2001` | `SCRAPE_FAILED` | Monitoring couldn't collect metrics from one agent. Usually the agent is paused or restarting. |
| `MON-2002` | `REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE` | Monitoring failed to reach the Registry API three times in a row. It raises the `RegistryUnreachable` alert. |
</source>

<source id="prometheus-server/prometheus_agent.md:6" doc="prometheus-server/prometheus_agent.md" title="Prometheus Agent Mode" section="Prometheus Agent Mode > Prometheus Agent Mode > How to Use Agent Mode in Detail" date="2026-09-26" type="vendor">
### How to Use Agent Mode in Detail

Use the `--agent` flag to run Prometheus in the Agent mode. The rest of the flags are either for both server and Agent or only for a specific mode. You can see which flag is for which mode by checking the last sentence of a flag's help string. "Use with server mode only" means it's only for server mode. If you don't see any mention like this, it means the flag is shared.

The Agent mode accepts the same scrape configuration with the same discovery options and remote write options. It also exposes a web UI on port 9095 with disabled query capabilities but shows build info, configuration, targets, and service discovery information as in a normal Prometheus server.
</source>

### How to Use Agent Mode in Detail

Use the `--agent` flag to run Prometheus in the Agent mode. The rest of the flags are either for both server and Agent or only for a specific mode. You can see which flag is for which mode by checking the last sentence of a flag's help string. "Use with server mode only" means it's only for server mode. If you don't see any mention like this, it means the flag is shared.

The Agent mode accepts the same scrape configuration with the same discovery options and remote write options. It also exposes a web UI on port 9095 with disabled query capabilities but shows build info, configuration, targets, and service discovery information as in a normal Prometheus server.

data for billing, and Prometheus for the rest of your monitoring.

## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

`claude-legacy` was deprecated in v2.5 and will be switched off on 2026-10-31. Any agent still on it that day stops answering. No new agent can be put on it: the registry returns `REG-1010`.
</source>

<source id="D07:4" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 3: Switch" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 3: Switch

Set the new model with `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}`. The change applies from each agent's next session.
</source>

<source id="D07:1" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Which agents are affected" date="2026-07-02" type="official">

As of this writing, two active agents are on `claude-legacy`:

| Agent | Owner | Target model |
|---|---|---|
| `research_agent` | research-team | `claude-sonnet` |
| `notes_agent` | support-team | `claude-haiku` |

Owners can check any agent with `GET /agents/{agent_id}` and look at its `model` field.
</source>

<source id="D07:5" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 4: Roll back if needed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 4: Roll back if needed

You can't roll back to `claude-legacy`: the registry refuses it. If the new model misbehaves, set the agent's `status` to `paused` while you fix the problem, and tell its users.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Errors

Every error response has the same shape:

```json
{"error": {"code": "REG-1007", "name": "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "message": "claude-opus is not allowed on tier standard"}}
```

The `code` is stable and safe to match on in code; the `message` is for people and may change. The full list is in the error code reference.
</source>

Based on the incident documentation for INC-2041, the **AgentErrorRateHigh** alert fired first at 06:02 for the billing_agent [D09:1].

According to the timeline:
- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.

This was the only alert explicitly mentioned in the incident summary, so AgentErrorRateHigh fired at 06:02, making it the first alert during this incident.

Based on the Monitoring guide documentation [D08:1], the **AgentErrorRateHigh** alert fires when **more than 5% of sessions end in an error over 15 minutes**.

To break it down:
- **Time window**: Measures over a 15-minute period
- **Threshold**: More than 5% session failure rate
- **What counts as an error**: Any session that ends with an error

This matches with what happened in INC-2041, where `billing_agent` was stuck making failed calls to payments-gateway, causing its error rate to exceed the 5% threshold and trigger the alert at 06:02.

## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

|---|---|

<source id="prometheus-docs/practices/the_zen.md:15" doc="prometheus-docs/practices/the_zen.md" title="The Zen of Prometheus" section="The Zen of Prometheus > Symptom-based alerts for paging, cause-based for troubleshooting" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## Symptom-based alerts for paging, cause-based for troubleshooting

Similar to Measure what users care about, alert on what *really* matters. It doesn't matter if your CPU is saturated, as long as your users don't notice. Let your SLOs guide your alerting.

Not every alert needs to page someone. Cause-based alerts shouldn't wake anyone up—they should feed into dashboards or ticket queues to be checked when needed or handled in batches at leisure. Reserve paging for symptom-based alerts that indicate user-facing impact.

For more context My Philosophy on Alerting.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/glossary.md:25" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/glossary.md" title="Glossary" section="Glossary > Target" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
### Target

A target is the definition of an object to scrape. For example, what labels to apply, any authentication required to connect, or other information that defines how the scrape will occur.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/practices/the_zen.md:2" doc="prometheus-docs/practices/the_zen.md" title="The Zen of Prometheus" section="The Zen of Prometheus > Measure what users care about" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## Measure what users care about

Do your users care if your database servers are down? Do they care about your CPU saturation? Yes, but not directly—they care about what they experience. They care about whether they can access the page they requested and whether their results are fresh. Think in terms of latencies and availability. Let your SLOs guide your instrumentation and alerting.

RED, USE and The Four Golden Signals are known frameworks to get you started.

You should still measure internal metrics like database availability and CPU saturation—use them for troubleshooting and capacity planning.

    Use causal metrics to answer why something is broken.
</source>

## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. </source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>
